name: olai-plugin-pi
//name: UNSCOPED, like every other tenant: `@olai/*` is the scope for the packages that ARE olai, and an ENGINE is somebody else's agent with olai's judgement about it on top — the closest thing in this tree to a plugin written outside it. The directory is the plugin word (`pi`), which is the row's `id`, the word `--plugins` takes, and the address of its docs page.
//exports: FIVE, and the split is the tree's three-door rule with nothing added. `./server` is what the row mounts: the leg, the pair of probes this row is (the pinned adapter from `OLAI_ACP_PI`, the wrapped agent from the search path), and the install sentence — no `solid-js` anywhere on that graph. `./browser` is the chunk the tab fetches when the roster names this plugin, and it carries TWO things and only one of them is a face: the MARK this engine wears in a transcript's speaker column (a `<g>`, which is genuinely this plugin's drawing), and its INSTALL SENTENCE for the panel's no-agent face (a `NotHere` VALUE — core draws every stroke of that row and this package writes every word of it). The ROOT is the wire identity and nothing more — this plugin composes no sibling surface. `./testids` and `./all.css` are the two contracts the generated bundle files need of every row.
//: THE PI ENGINE — the leg that reads pi-acp's wire, the pair of halves that make a pi row (a pinned adapter olai ships, an agent the machine has), and the mark it wears. `acp/` beside this manifest is the adapter's own pin and the patch it carries, which travelled here with the phase: the pin and the patches of an engine live in that engine's directory.
//dependencies: `@olai/acp/engine` is the shape both ends spell — the leg, the adapter, the registration — and it is a floor package under both this plugin and `olai-plugin-chat`, which is what lets neither import the other. `@olai/plugin-api` is the door: the `Agents` tag its `./server` registers into, and the slot service its `./browser` hangs a mark in. `effect` because a plugin's `apply` is one. `solid-js` because the mark is a component. NO protocol SDK, not even in the bench: this leg's own signatures name none of its types and its bench stages payloads rather than permission options.
